etymologies.etymologyHTML: Borrowed from Ancient Greek νέον (néon), neuter of νέος (néos, “new”), from earlier *νέϝος (*néwos), from Proto-Hellenic *newos, from Proto-Indo-European *néwos.

definitions.definition: (uncountable) The chemical element (symbol Ne) with an atomic number of 10. The second of the noble gases, it is a colourless, odorless inert gas.
(countable) A form or sample of the element.
(countable, uncountable) Neon signs or lights, collectively.

quote.citation: 1970, “Up Around the Bend”, performed by Creedence Clearwater Revival:
quote.text: Bring a song and a smile for the banjoBetter get while the getting's goodHitch a ride to the end of the highwayWhere the neons turn to wood

quote.citation: 2009, Jason Syner, How to Install Automotive Mobile Electronic Systems, page 27:
quote.text: Neons and LED lighting can be controlled by remotes.

definitions.definition: (of a color) That resembles a neon light; extremely bright; fluorescent
